chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from 'Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father

Regarding a man who made it upon himself for the sake of God the freeing of a slave, and he freed a lame or a cripple, he (the Imam) said: 'If he is among those who are sold, it suffices for him, unless he had specified him, then upon him is what he stipulated and named.'
ai.seo_question: Does freeing a defective slave satisfy a vow to free a slave?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the principle of specificity in vows (nadhr) is clarified: if a person vows to free a 'slave' generally, any slave suffices, but if they specify a particular individual, that exact person must be freed regardless of defects. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the literal intent of the vow-maker, ensuring that the fulfillment matches the precise commitment made to Allah. It highlights the balance between ease in general vows and strict adherence in specific ones, reflecting the broader legal maxim that vows are binding contracts with divine obligations.
